newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup to place aircraft in lease unit.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup to place aircraft in lease unit.

text.p: SAirGroup said it would transfer its aircraft into a newly-founded subsidiary Flightlease AG to better manage its fleet of aircraft.
In a first step, SAirGroup said in a statement that Swissair -- the core airline in the group -- would transfer 25 of its aircraft into the leasing unit.
During the second half of the year, Flightlease will also take over the current leasing contracts for other Swissair aircraft. Swissair's fleet consists of 62 aircraft.
The transaction is valued at more than 2.5 billion Swiss francs ($1.7 billion) and is part of SAirGroup's strategy of splitting itself into independent profit centres to improve transparency.
The move would not affect any book profits that SAirGroup makes from selling aircraft because Flightlease is 100-percent owned by the group, a SAirGroup spokesman said.

SAirGroup's statement said the advantages from the move include an optimal utilisation of the aircraft's value by concentrating know-how from aircraft purchases and the access to advantageous purchase and financing models.
The spokesman said the aircraft operated by charter unit Charter Leisure would also be taken over by Flightlease.
There were no specific plans for transferring the aircraft owned by regional airline Crossair AG into Flightlease, but "that is an option," he added.
Flighlease is headed by Hans-Joerg Hunziker, chief financial officer of SAirServices, and board chairman is Philippe Bruggisser, chief executive of SAirGroup.
